judgments.catchwords: Appeal - Appeal against the High Court Order of “Minimum Wage Order” - the employees had to establish the value of their entitlement and any actual deductions from wages or related payments. judgments.title: TANG SIEW LAN & ors v ONG KIAN FAR & ors

parties.label: DEFENDAN
names: TANG NGE AI @ TANG NG KING

judgments.catchwords: Res judicata – bar against re litigation of issues conclusively determined in prior proceedings. Express trust validity – three certainties of intention, subject matter, and object satisfied. Probate and Administration Act 1959 – Section 60 sanction; administrator’s powers; judicial validation. Limitation Act 1953 – twelve year statutory bar; Section 22(1) exception inapplicable to non beneficiaries. Doctrine of laches – inordinate delay defeating equitable relief. Admissions of liability – evidential weight; cannot override final judgments; suspicion of perjury. Locus standi – exclusion of plaintiffs as beneficiaries; lack of standing to challenge trust. Constructive trust – express trust supersedes remedial constructive trust; no unconscionable conduct. Order 18 rule 19 – striking out pleadings; plain and obvious cases; abuse of process. Appropriation and reprobation – impermissible contradictory reliance on trust principles. Administrator’s fiduciary duties – limits of authority; breach claims as collateral attack. Family trust disputes – preservation of ancestral lands; intra family litigation.
judgments.judge: YA Puan Shoba Rajah a/p Dorai Rajah

judgments.title: SIVACHANDRAN A/L S JAYARAJAH v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Review jurisdiction - Rule 137 of the Rules of the Federal Court 1995 -Inherent powers of Federal Court – All sentences passed to be in accordance with the law – Avoiding miscarriage of justice - Exceptional circumstances - Fresh evidence of prisoner’s death following whipping. Judicial whipping - Corporal punishment - Whether judicial whipping amounts to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment (“CIDT”) - Whether punishment of whipping is inconsistent with constitutional protection of life, dignity and bodily integrity. Whether whipping is disproportionate and therefore contrary to Article 8(1) - Whether exemption of women from whipping constitutes prohibited discrimination on ground only of gender is contrary to Art 8(2) - Intelligible differentia. Whether whipping is against Art. 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (“UDHR”) and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration in its prohibitions against CIDT - Whether whipping is against customary international law.
